content.value:
ROUND-2 PRODUCT CALL, FOR THE LEAD, NOT A BUILDER. cch-w53-s1 makes the console honest; it deliberately does not decide the feature's future. Three options, with the measurement that reorders them.

THE MEASUREMENT THAT CHANGES THE ARGUMENT: prod env_vars has ZERO rows (n_live_tup=0, n_tup_ins=0, n_tup_del=0 since the 2026-07-23 postmaster start) against 27 teams / 27 users / 8 barkparks, and the sanity totals in the same query prove the zero is data, not a broken query. There are NO persisted encrypted user rows. Every 'user data at risk' argument for deferring is unsupported. AND THERE IS NO STAGING: staging.barkpark.cloud is NXDOMAIN (ANSWER: 0, curl 000, while barkpark.cloud returns 200), the control-plane host runs ONE app database (barkpark_cloud_prod) and the live control plane points at exactly it. A drop migration has exactly one target and it is empty.

THE PRECEDENT: D360 (producerless general -> DELETE) and D589 (api transport -> DELETE not disclose) both ruled on measured write-silence. This is the same evidentiary shape, only more so: not merely producerless but zero rows ever. The precedent points at DELETE. What still makes it a lead call is product intent — a shipped, documented Coolify-parity feature with a full CRUD surface and a working encryption seam — not data.

OPTION A, DELETE. Blast radius measured: 3 routes (router.ex:4488/4509/4573), 22 envVars/env-var//v1/env-vars occurrences in app.js, 26 registry.ex hits, env_var.ex, two dedicated test files, one audit_event.ex verb pair, and the claim key. Vercel's env_vars (vercel/real.ex:44-86) is a DIFFERENT feature and must not be swept. Under D594's ordering law the code deploy that stops reading env_vars ships FIRST and the drop table is a later, separate migration.
OPTION B, STORE-ONLY WITH HONEST COPY (what s1 ships). Honest, but still promise-shaped: the screen accepts a live production secret, encrypts it, lists it forever, and does nothing with it. The user's ACT is unchanged. Defensible only if the input is disabled or explicitly labelled not-delivered.
OPTION C, BUILD INJECTION — and it is SMALLER than previously believed, which is the load-bearing correction. The plane ALREADY has a shipped, control-plane-initiated mechanism that writes a key into a live box's /opt/barkpark/.env and restarts the app: internal/provisioner/attach_domain.go:18 const attachEnvFile = "/opt/barkpark/.env", merge steps :158-230, restart step :225 ('pick up BARKPARK_EXTRA_ORIGINS'), wired :306, driven by registry.ex:1072 enqueue -> :1274 claim -> :2087 succeed. support.go:1008-1011 rewrites the same file for BARKPARK_ALLOW_BUNDLE_IMPORT. So the honest sentence is NOT 'the plane has no mechanism' but 'the mechanism exists for the plane's OWN keys and the advertised user surface is not wired to it'. That removes the 'we would have to build it from scratch' escape.
BUT COUNT OPTION C'S REAL COSTS: (1) BARKPARK_EXTRA_ORIGINS is a PLANE-chosen key; wiring arbitrary USER key=value through an attach-domain-style shell heredoc crosses a NEW trust boundary, which is exactly why attach_domain.go carries defensive regexes. (2) The six-name provisioner scrubber that D595 called a COMPLETE cover of worker-held secrets stops being complete — every step that sources .env can echo arbitrary user keys. (3) Key collision with BARKPARK_* has no policy. (4) Provision-time-only injection CANNOT honour 'every instance': the 8 existing boxes never receive it, so that label stays false until an apply-to-running path plus a redeploy-required / last-applied surface exists — the Vercel/Render/Kinsta bar, and a second feature rather than a field.

WHATEVER IS ORDERED: it is a MIGRATION and the lead orders it (standing rule). Do not let a builder ship a schema change unannounced.
